title: The diagonal ideal is invertible
statement: For every scheme $S$, let $P=\mathbf P^1_S$ [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change] and let $\Delta:P\to P\times_SP$ be the diagonal [def-pc-fibre-product]. Then the kernel ideal sheaf of $\Delta$ is invertible in the sense of [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal]: locally on $P\times_SP$ it is generated by one nonzerodivisor.

source.place: Worker decomposition of the diagonal integral proof

proof.text: $P\to S$ is separated, being proper [lemma-nagata-projective-space-base-change-proper], and smooth of relative dimension one (on each standard open it is the affine line). Hence its diagonal is a regular immersion of pure codimension one [lem-pur-diagonal-regular-immersion]. Around every point the ideal is then generated by a weakly regular sequence of length one [def-pur-regular-immersion]; a one-term weakly regular sequence is a nonzerodivisor, so the ideal is locally principal on a nonzerodivisor.

source.place: Proof, first two sentences: the diagonal is an effective Cartier divisor (replacing the four-chart computation by the regular-immersion criterion)
